title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The code nothing in the project reaches
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.40.0 finds the classes, objects and functions that nothing in the whole project references, the first check here that reasons across files rather than within one.

highlights.title: Across Files, Not Within One
highlights.description: "Find Unreferenced Symbols" covers top-level classes, objects, interfaces, functions and properties. On a 3444 file project it found 89, every one confirmed by hand, in under two seconds.

highlights.title: The Imports Come With It
highlights.description: Removing a declaration leaves imports dangling in other files, and the project stops compiling. The fix deletes those too, and deletes the whole file when nothing else is left in it.

highlights.title: Tests Get Their Own Category
highlights.description: A symbol only the tests reference is reported separately and never offered for removal: deleting one breaks the test that exercises it. The quick fix suggests @VisibleForTesting instead.

sections.heading: Improvements
bullets: Adds "Kotlin Jump: Find Unreferenced Symbols" and "Remove All Unreferenced Symbols", the second clearing everything with a safe fix in one Refactor Preview.
Deletes the whole file when nothing but the dead declaration is left in it. On the project measured above that applied to 42 files.
Counts a reference wherever it really is: manifests, layouts, navigation graphs, Gradle scripts, ProGuard rules, META-INF/services entries and plain string literals.
Keeps alive anything named only by an aliased import or by a fully qualified call with no import, which a per-symbol search would miss.
Never reports a symbol carrying an annotation outside a short benign list, extending an Android or Gradle type anywhere up the chain, or declared more than once.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Fixes comment stripping inside a multi-line raw string, where a later // blanked live content and could hide a real reference.
